staleCellKinds.//: The ONLY evidence kinds allowed to be stale, and the half of this gate that a bare count cannot give. A count alone is satisfied by swapping one stale cell for another: clear a perf cell, let a browser-matrix cell go stale, and 22 is still 22 while the matrix now hides a lane that quietly stopped running. A stale cell of any kind not named here is an ERROR whatever the count says, and the message names the component and the kind. Add a kind here only with the reason it cannot be re-run, never to make a red run green.

evidenceCells.//: RESIDUAL-17, closing D-RES16-3 option (a). The TWO-WAY, PER-KIND record of every `pass` and `present` cell -- the numbers this repository quotes as its evidence. `validate:capability-matrix` gate 8 fails when a kind's count RISES and when it FALLS, because unlike a ceiling neither direction is free here: a rise can be a loosened predicate crediting cells nothing exercised (RESIDUAL-16 measured exactly that -- `storyCheck` published 27 `state-stories` cells as `pass` because a component the check never ASKED was absent from the failing set), and a fall can be a regression quietly dropping real evidence. RESIDUAL-16 removed 42 false cells, 27 of them `pass`, and `yarn validate:all` exited 0 with 53 green links and no red one, because nothing in this repository held either number. Per KIND rather than in total, for the reason `staleCellKinds` exists: 558 is also satisfied by trading 27 real passes for 27 invented ones in another column.
evidenceCells.//declaring-a-move: A legitimate move is ONE edit to the kind's entry below, in the same change that moves the number -- the same handshake `staleCells.ceiling` uses. It is deliberately cheap, because an honest audit must not be expensive: RESIDUAL-16 rightly LOWERED `pass` by 27 and future audits will do the same. So the gate does the arithmetic for you -- it names the kind, the state, the direction and the delta, and prints the corrected `kinds` block ready to paste. What it will not do is move the number itself; the record is the place a reader looks to see that a withdrawal was declared rather than absorbed. Write WHY in the `//moves` log below when you change one, never to make a red run green.

2026-10-06 DZUP-UI-R6-01-20261006-R1: present 526 -> 532 (+6), keyboard-spec +3 and controlled-uncontrolled +3. DzTree dispatches Space (select, deselect, default prevented), DzMention dispatches ArrowUp (moves the highlight, wraps, inserts the wrapped option; inert while the menu is closed), DzOrderList dispatches Home (focus first row; grabbed row to the top) and Enter (selects/deselects in a selectable list, inert otherwise). Each of the three drives both model paths: a parent binding with an update listener that renders only what it writes back and wins on replacement, and an unbound or one-way value the component owns locally. Tree and OrderList use named models (`selectedKeys`, `value`); the spec comment that names `update:modelValue` explains that, and the tests assert the named event. Human AT, axe, portal and Tab-only cells of these components are not touched. Perf pass and stale counters remain the inherited main drift.
